title: PHP Dies After Every Request. How the Zend Engine Actually Runs Your Code.
why_read: This is a genuinely detailed architectural walkthrough of how the Zend Engine handles PHP's shared-nothing model, OPcache, zvals, and JIT, well above the typical Dev.to fare.
analysis: PHP's shared-nothing architecture means every request gets a fresh process or thread with no persistent state, which eliminates whole classes of concurrency bugs at the cost of repeated initialization overhead. The article explains how OPcache short-circuits that overhead by caching compiled bytecode in shared memory across requests. It also covers zvals, the 16-byte internal value representation PHP uses, and how copy-on-write reduces unnecessary memory duplication. The tracing JIT, added in PHP 8, compiles hot execution paths to native machine code, and the article places all of these pieces together in a coherent architectural picture.
